sections.html:
Cheshire is a New Haven County town in the Naugatuck Valley planning region, 14 miles north of New Haven and 25 miles south of Hartford. It spans 33.4 square miles, nearly all land, at about 230 feet of elevation. Waterbury is next door, and the town also borders Southington, Meriden, Wallingford, Hamden, Bethany, Prospect and Wolcott.

The 2020 census counted 28,733 residents in 10,169 households and 10,401 housing units. Median household income was $120,546 in 2019. A town manager runs a council-manager government, and because New Haven, Hartford, Waterbury and Meriden are all a short drive away, commute times come up at nearly every showing. Cheshire Village, a census-designated place within the town, had 6,499 residents in 2020. Buyers who tour here are generally weighing a quiet, car-based town against the shorter commute they could get in a city, so a clear description of your street and how long it takes to reach the highway helps them decide.

The town was first settled in 1694 and incorporated in May 1780. What matters to a seller is the postwar boom. Population stayed under about 4,400 until 1940, then reached 6,295 in 1950 and 13,383 in 1960, a rise of 112.6 percent in a single decade.

That pace points to heavy building around mid-century. Find out from an inspector what shape the roof, wiring and heating system are in, ideally before a buyer's inspector does.

Most trips here are by car. Interstate 691 skirts the northern edge and Interstate 84 clips the northwest corner.

  • Route 10: the main north-south road, the busiest, and full of stoplights.
  • Routes 68 and 70: east-west through Main Street and West Main Street.
  • Route 42: a second east-west road.
  • CTtransit 229: bus service between Waterbury and New Haven along Routes 70 and 10.
  • Commuter express bus: from a lot near Interstate 84 to Hartford.

Route 10 between Routes 68/70 and Route 42 backs up on weekday mornings and evenings, and again when the high school lets out around 2 p.m. If your street is on or near Route 10, a buyer will notice, so describe the noise level honestly.

Two areas are on the National Register: the Cheshire Historic District around Main Street and the Marion Historic District. The Farmington Canal Lock at 487 North Brooksvale Road and the First Congregational Church are listed too. A town office can confirm whether your lot sits in a district, which matters before any exterior work.

The Farmington Canal Heritage Trail crosses town, and Roaring Brook Falls in the southwest corner is Connecticut's tallest single-drop waterfall. Listings near the trail or the parks often lean on those details.

sections.h2: Weather and what it does to a house
sections.html:
Cheshire is inland, with about 54.6 inches of precipitation a year. January highs average 35 degrees and lows 15, and July highs reach 83, so heating, insulation and the roof all get a workout.

Buyers' inspectors here go over the roof, gutters, basement dampness, the heating system and exterior wood. If you have service records for the boiler or furnace and the roof, dig them out now.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax at a Cheshire closing
sections.html:
Any deed for $2,000 or more triggers Connecticut's conveyance tax. At recording, Form OP-236 goes in from the seller, the seller's lawyer or an authorized agent, using 025 as the Cheshire town code.

Piece of the sale priceConveyance rate
State, most homesthree-quarters of one percent
State, residential estate portion from $800,000 up to $2.5 million1.25 percent
State, residential estate portion above $2.5 million2.25 percent
Town of Cheshireone-fourth of one percent

Some transfers are exempt, such as those between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence. Should a tax bill be open, a payoff figure lets the closing take it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Crumbling foundations and the closing paperwork
sections.html:
A failing foundation can change the tax filing. The Department of Revenue Services treats a principal residence whose concrete foundation has deteriorated from pyrrhotite, as a professional engineer determines, as an exempt conveyance. Only the first transfer after the engineer's written evaluation qualifies, and the evaluation travels with the return. Owners receiving money from the Crumbling Foundations Assistance Fund are shut out.

If you suspect trouble, get the evaluation first. It affects both the price and the closing documents.

sections.h2: How a direct sale works in Cheshire
sections.html:
Cash sales help owners in a hurry, heirs with an un-updated house and landlords ready to leave. They help less with a fully updated house that would likely attract several retail offers.

  1. Give us the address, the condition, any tenants and the timeline you are working with.
  2. Our offer comes back for the house as it stands.
  3. Accepting it sends the deed and the tax return to a title company or attorney.
  4. Proceeds cover taxes and liens first, and the rest is yours.

Compare what each route nets after commission, repairs, carrying costs and time. We will give you our view of the house, and if listing makes more sense, we will say so.

Preparation shortens the path to a closing date. Pull the deed, or estate papers if an owner has died, so the title company can confirm who may sign. Get a payoff from the Tax Collector and one from each mortgage lender. If the house has a tenant, find the lease.

Then walk the house the way a buyer's inspector will. Look at the roof, the basement, the boiler and any wood on the outside. Anything you find is cheaper to know now than to hear about in week three of a contract. If the repairs are more than you want to take on, that is when a direct sale tends to come up.

Whichever way you sell, ask for every figure in writing, including your estimated net, so the options can be compared fairly, and keep the written copies with your closing papers. Do this before you sign anything. That habit protects you from a high headline number that shrinks once commission, repairs and carrying costs come out. It also gives your attorney something concrete to review.

Assessed values come from the Cheshire Assessor, and the Tax Collector sends bills and takes payments. A call to each gets you current rates, due dates and a payoff figure. The town's school office can tell you which school serves your street, and the town can tell you which historic district, if any, covers your address.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance tax in Cheshire?
faqs.a: Three-quarters of one percent goes to the state on most homes, with one-fourth of one percent for the town. Higher state rates reach residential estates above $800,000 and nonresidential property.

faqs.q: Does a pyrrhotite foundation affect a Cheshire sale?
faqs.a: It can. With an engineer's written evaluation attached to the return, a principal residence damaged by pyrrhotite may qualify for an exempt conveyance.
Cheshire High School, Dodd Middle School and four elementary schools: Chapman, Doolittle, Highland and Barnum. The town's school office can tell you which one serves your street.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cheshire house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Direct buyers take a house as it is and build repairs into the price, whereas a listed house that needs work can mean repair credits after the inspection.

faqs.q: Who sets property taxes in Cheshire?
faqs.a: Assessed values come from the Assessor, while the Tax Collector issues and collects the bills. Both offices can give you the current rate, due dates and a payoff figure.
